change.title: Explicit shard grants for svc_bundle_reader
change.diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/db/migrations/0042_reader_shard_grants.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+-- Make the reader's access to shard databases explicit so per-principal
+-- query limits and audit logging apply to it.
+GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader;

verdict.headline: Explicit shard grants double data exposure for svc_bundle_reader, exceeding worker-runtime startup limit
verdict.cause:
The change adds GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader. In the candidate run, this gave svc_bundle_reader access to r0.* tables in addition to the default database, doubling the rows visible from 90 to 180. The bundle-builder produced a bundle with 180 entries, and worker-runtime refused to start because it preallocates 150 entries, observing: "bundle has 180 entries but the runtime preallocates 150; refusing to start" (exit code 2).

Evidence chain:
- Baseline experiment x-d3fae9d9456d4975: 90 rows_visible_to_builder, 90 bundle-builder.entries, worker-runtime.exit_code=0 with GRANT SELECT ON default.* only
- Candidate experiment x-e860ff8b8bf44ddf: 180 rows_visible_to_builder, 180 bundle-builder.entries, worker-runtime.exit_code=2 with both GRANT SELECT ON default.* and GRANT SELECT ON r0.* added
- Second baseline x-f808dbc5c8844234: confirmed exit_code=0 with default-only grants
- Dependency path: change → grants on database r0 → principal svc_bundle_reader → service bundle-builder → reads bundle_fields → artifact bundle.json → loaded by worker-runtime

The explicit shard grant doubles data exposure, causing the bundle size to exceed the worker-runtime preallocation limit of 150 entries.
tested: x-d3fae9d9456d4975: baseline · workload default → all assertions passed
x-e860ff8b8bf44ddf: candidate · workload default → failed: runtime_starts_with_bundle
x-a156d29e6aca4365: candidate · workload default → failed: runtime_starts_with_bundle
x-edb5eeb719ed4e00: control · workload default → all assertions passed
x-f808dbc5c8844234: baseline · workload default → all assertions passed
limitations: Independent review was unavailable for this run.

The runtime_setting rc-0014 has setting_key=startup_timeout_s=30 (not a preallocation limit). The 150-entry preallocation limit was observed in the candidate experiment logs ("bundle has 180 entries but the runtime preallocates 150"); its originating setting_id was not retrieved before budget exhaustion. No direct observation of per-principal query limits in meta-store.

mitigation.text: Remove the GRANT SELECT ON r0.* line from migration 0042, or increase the worker-runtime preallocation limit to accommodate 180+ entries. The minimal fix is to omit the r0.* grant, keeping only the default.* grant that was in place before the change.
